questions.q: What is LOAD CSV in Neo4j?
options: A Cypher clause that reads a CSV file row by row to create nodes and relationships in a running database
A standalone command-line tool that runs while the database is offline
A GUI wizard inside Neo4j Desktop
A tool exclusive to Neo4j Aura
questions.explain: LOAD CSV is run like any other Cypher query, reading a file row by row and using each row's values in the rest of the query.

questions.q: Why is MERGE typically preferred over CREATE when importing data with LOAD CSV?
options: MERGE only creates a node if a matching one doesn't already exist by a given key, making the import safely re-runnable
MERGE is faster than CREATE in every situation
CREATE cannot be used inside LOAD CSV at all
MERGE automatically deletes duplicate nodes after import
questions.explain: Using MERGE avoids creating duplicate nodes if the import is run more than once, unlike CREATE which always creates a new node.

questions.q: What problem does `CALL { ... } IN TRANSACTIONS` solve when used with LOAD CSV?
options: It batches a large import into smaller transactions to avoid exhausting memory on one enormous transaction
It encrypts the CSV file during import
It automatically converts CSV data into JSON
It removes the need for a CSV header row
questions.explain: For genuinely large files, batching the work into smaller transactions (e.g. 1000 rows at a time) is the standard pattern to avoid memory issues.

questions.q: When is `neo4j-admin database import` the right tool to use instead of LOAD CSV?
options: For a one-time initial load of a very large dataset, before the database is live
For small incremental updates to a database that's already serving live traffic
Whenever using Neo4j Aura instead of a local install
Only when importing from a relational database directly, never from CSV
questions.explain: neo4j-admin database import builds store files directly while the database is offline, making it much faster for a first bulk load but unsuitable for incremental updates.

questions.q: What must be true of the CSV files used with `neo4j-admin database import`?
options: They must be pre-shaped into Neo4j's expected node/relationship format, typically with a header file describing columns
They must be converted to XML first
They can be in any arbitrary, unstructured format
They must already exist as Neo4j database files, not CSV
questions.explain: Unlike LOAD CSV's flexible row-by-row Cypher processing, neo4j-admin import expects CSVs pre-shaped to its specific node/relationship format.
